{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABZkMWiA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhDK0qo", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 71, "title": "Correct V9938 interlaced field timing across core, Wasm and browser scheduling", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `8aaeffdf863896cc56d1f80e5af2c09080124761`, `crates/msx-core/src/vdp.rs::tick()` and `frame_cycles()` use progressive 262/313-line budgets even when R9.IL enables interlace. Rendering already weaves fields, while S#2.EO derives from the incorrectly timed field counter. `Machine::frame()`, `msx_frame_cycles()` and `web/app.js::frameMilliseconds()` consume those budgets.

Interlaced workloads therefore accumulate incorrect emulated time, field parity and browser/audio cadence. Compatibility impact is inferred; no commercial-title failure was observed.

## Expected outcome

Implement V9938 half-line field scheduling and consistent consumers, including the phase handling necessary for existing rendering, status and interrupts. At the existing six-master-clocks-per-CPU-cycle ratio:

| Timing | Progressive CPU cycles | Interlaced CPU cycles per VSYNC field |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| NTSC | 59,736 | 59,850 |
| PAL | 71,364 | 71,250 |

Two interlaced fields total 119,700/142,500 CPU cycles respectively. Preserve horizontal phase across field boundaries and distinguish VSYNC field duration from active-display spacing.

## Context

The clean checkout matches inspected GitHub main. The open Issue/PR collection is empty. [Issue #67](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/issues/67) explicitly deferred interlace half-lines; earlier addressing and command corrections do not resolve them.

Inspected references:

- [Yamaha V9938 Technical Data Book](https://www.dinoboards.com.au/assets/video-v9958/yamaha_v9938.pdf), printed pages 5, 10, 103 and 146–147: IL/EO controls, field identification and timing tables. Both fields have the fractional durations above; the second field’s top erase interval increases by half a line. Map these tables onto the emulator’s display-relative origin explicitly. The tables apply at R18=0; they do not establish every register-transition edge.
- [Pinned openMSX VDP.cc](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/video/VDP.cc), `frameStart()`, and [VDP.hh](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/video/VDP.hh), `getTicksPerFrame()`: useful field-state references, but they retain integer-line budgets and explicitly provisional fixation/parity timing. They are not an exact timing oracle. V9958-only counter observations must not be presented as V9938 confirmation.

Existing `tests/msx2.rs` covers weaving and progressive PAL transitions; `tests/fetch_timing.rs` covers progressive budgets/overshoot; `tests/vdp_fh.rs` covers FH phases. Inspected [CI logs](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/actions/runs/40072912733/job/120810023701) report 291 Rust and 200 browser passes, including those timing cases. Their presence and passing results do not validate interlaced timing. Planning executed no builds or tests.

Scope includes necessary cross-file scheduling, rendering/status integration, original diagnostics and documentation. Full vertical-counter/overscan reconstruction, VRAM arbitration and unrelated command/audio corrections remain separate work.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement the stated stable progressive/interlaced budgets for both 192/212-line configurations. Process partial lines and multiple crossed fields without dropping or duplicating elapsed time. Preserve continuous horizontal phase; do not obtain half-line timing by inserting a shortened visible scanline.
- [ ] Document the mapping between VSYNC field origin and the existing display-relative raster. Represent the manufacturer’s alternating field phase coherently in active rendering, S#2.EO and existing vertical/horizontal event scheduling. Demonstrate both field parities, IL with EO off/on, page selection and 384/424-row weaving without stale, skipped or duplicated rows. Retain FH polling, enable and acknowledgement conventions and independent VBlank acknowledgement.
- [ ] Adopt an explicit approximation for unresolved NT/IL fixation: writes before the first tick configure the initial field; subsequent changes take effect at the next field boundary, with the latest pending values winning. Use consistent active timing/display state across consumers. Writes must not reset elapsed time or resurrect interrupts. Label this policy as selected behavior, not measured silicon behavior; update incompatible progressive-transition expectations with an explanation. Cover direct/indirect writes, repeated switches, reset and model changes.
- [ ] Add independent native boundary and sequence tests with literal expectations before/at/after field edges, two-field phase relationships and at least 100-field totals of 5,985,000 NTSC and 7,125,000 PAL CPU cycles. Compare bulk and irregular tick partitions, including carried half-lines. Record meaningful failures against the baseline and corrected results; avoid expectations calculated with production helpers.
- [ ] Extend Machine tests to relate actual CPU T-states, bounded instruction overshoot/debt, field events and cumulative PCM sample counts. Keep FDC, cassette, RTC, PSG/SCC/FM and command advancement tied to executed CPU cycles. Ensure Wasm’s advertised scheduling budget and the browser accumulator agree through timing transitions without double-counting or discarding emulated time.
- [ ] Add an independently authored CPU port/status probe and compiled-Wasm browser coverage at `/` and `/msx-rust/`. Observe interlaced parity/timing, Canvas weaving, budget transitions and PCM totals using existing instrumentation. Include deterministic animation-frame scheduling observations so browser pacing is exercised beyond manually calling Wasm. Require no proprietary firmware, ROMs or human gameplay.
- [ ] Preserve existing MSX1/MSX2, audio, disk, SRAM retention/persistence, firmware/slot, input, Wasm/browser lifecycle and ownership/provenance behavior where affected. Update affected timing documentation and fixtures without weakening unrelated coverage.
- [ ] Before merge, the Coordinator runs and reports README checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, `npm test` and `git diff --check`, with documented dependency setup as needed. Complete source-Issue/full-diff review and resolve blocking findings. Distinguish passed, failed, skipped and unperformed checks.

## Optional validation

Before merge, compare timestamped original diagnostic traces with available V9938 hardware recordings or a pinned upstream implementation, recording its timing approximations. Already lawfully available software may supplement these checks. These comparisons were not performed during planning; diagnostic success does not establish commercial playability.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
